# omni_document_permission (Resource)

Grants a content role on a document to users or groups.

The documents API has no endpoint for revoking a permission, so destroying this resource sets the role to `NO_ACCESS` rather than removing the entry.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omni_document_permission" "board_pack_viewers" {
  document_id = "abc123de"
  role        = "VIEWER"

  user_group_ids = [omni_user_group.executives.id]
}

# Like folder permissions, one resource per role, and the sets are
# authoritative for the role they name.
resource "omni_document_permission" "board_pack_editors" {
  document_id = "abc123de"
  role        = "EDITOR"

  user_ids = [
    omni_user.head_of_finance.id,
    omni_user.chief_of_staff.id,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `document_id` (String) The document identifier to grant access to.
- `role` (String) The content role to grant. One of `NO_ACCESS`, `VIEWER`, `EXPLORER`, `EDITOR`, `MANAGER` or `OWNER`. `OWNER` can only be granted to users, never to groups. These are content roles, which decide who can see and edit a folder or document. They are separate from model roles, which decide who can query data.

### Optional

- `access_boost` (Boolean) Whether to grant access boost alongside the role. Rejected with 403 when the organization has AccessBoost turned off.
- `user_group_ids` (Set of String) User group IDs granted this role. Authoritative for this resource. For embed, this is usually what you want: the `groups` claim in a signed URL resolves to these groups.

  Use the ID from `omni_user_group`, which is the SCIM miniUuid. Reading permissions back requires an extra lookup per group, because the permissions endpoint reports a group's full UUID instead and the two cannot be compared directly.
- `user_ids` (Set of String) User IDs granted this role. Authoritative for this resource: a user removed from the set has the grant revoked.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID in the form `<target id>:<role>`.
